ok, it took me some time
but I have finally made one research regarding "influence of different pages for vtes"
I have use my previous survey. It has more than 1000 answers and one of the tools was to track the refference page that linked to the survey.

So below you can find data regarding number of reference entrances to the survey from different web pages:

From my perspective data are solid. My conclusion is simple. At the moment we can reach more than 70% of "semi-active vtes users" using 3 main web adresses.

1) vekn.net
2) facebook.com
3) vtesone.wordpress.com/

Other have no influence at the moment.

Next issue is to reach to potential (new) players. I dont have any possibility to asses this.

www.boardgamegeek.com looks like the only reasonable but still very weak.

VEKN Marketing CoDirector

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
Interesting data from the language point of view:

English sites: 73.62%
French: 7.52%
Polish: 4.05%
Italian: 2.31%
Czech: 1.50%
Spanish: 1.27%
Russian: 0.93%
Hungarian: 0.81%
Finnish: 0.58%

The survey itself was in English, so the results are biased towards English speaking players. By comparing those results with another indicator of national activity, i.e. the number of tournaments held or the attendance to the NC, you might be able to detect if a community is under-represented because of the language bias. I have a gut feeling that the Spanish at least are missing, maybe the Brazilian too. I guess the Swedes all speak English anyway.
